lessons.title: At the train station
lessons.goal: Buy a ticket and ask about trains, platforms and connections.

tip.title: Dative after mit, von, nach, zu
tip.body: After mit, von, nach and zu you use the dative: mit dem Zug, von welchem Gleis. Separable verbs split in a main clause: abfahren → Der Zug fährt um zehn ab. Pronounce Zug as 'tsook' — z is always 'ts' and a final g sounds like k.

tip.title: müssen: verb to the end
tip.body: With a modal verb like müssen, the second verb goes to the end as an infinitive: Ich muss um elf Uhr auschecken. Questions start with the question word: Bis wann muss ich auschecken? For ü in Frühstück, say 'ee' and round your lips as if to whistle.

lessons.title: mit dem Zug, in die Stadt
lessons.goal: Use the dative after prepositions and tell wo? from wohin?

tip.title: Dative prepositions & two-way prepositions
tip.body: mit, zu, von, aus, bei and nach always take the dative: mit dem Bus, mit der U-Bahn, zur Arbeit (zu der). Two-way prepositions like in, an, auf, vor take the dative for wo? (in der Stadt, im Park) and the accusative for wohin? (in die Stadt, in den Park).

lessons.goal: Follow a conversation about a delayed train.

story.title: Cologne to Berlin
story.intro: Mia and Paul are waiting at Cologne station for their train to Berlin.

lines.name: Mia
lines.t: Paul, schau mal! Unser Zug hat dreißig Minuten Verspätung.
lines.n: Paul, look! Our train is thirty minutes late.

lines.name: Paul
lines.t: Oh nein! Dann verpassen wir in Hannover den Anschluss.
lines.n: Oh no! Then we'll miss the connection in Hanover.

lines.name: Mia
lines.t: Warte, eine Durchsage. Der Zug fährt heute von Gleis neun.
lines.n: Wait, an announcement. Today the train leaves from platform nine.

lines.name: Paul
lines.t: Von Gleis neun? Na super. Typisch Bahn!
lines.n: From platform nine? Great. Typical railway!

lines.name: Mia
lines.t: Keine Panik. Der Zug kommt erst in vierzig Minuten.
lines.n: Don't panic. The train only comes in forty minutes.

lines.name: Paul
lines.t: Gut. Dann kaufe ich noch zwei Kaffee.
lines.n: Good. Then I'll buy two coffees.

culture.title: Deutsche Bahn and punctuality
culture.body: Germans love joking about Deutsche Bahn: long-distance trains are often late, so Verspätung and Anschluss verpasst are everyday words. From 60 minutes late you can claim 25% of the fare back (50% from 120 minutes) — but only when the delay is the railway's fault, not force majeure such as storms (EU rules since 2023). Swiss trains (SBB) are famously punctual, and in Austria the ÖBB runs the network.
